PART I
SUPERVISION OF ELECTIONS

3. The Election Commission may, subject to the provisions
of Clause (1) of Article 115 of the Constitution, appoint a
Supervisor of Elections and a Deputy Supervisor of Elections
for each State, and a returning officer and so many assistant
returning officers for eath constituency as the Commission
may consider necessary.

4, (1) A Supervisor of Elections of a State appointed under
section 3 shall, subject to\the general direction and control
of the Election Commissipn, have all the powers and may
perform all the duties of the Commission in relation to the
conduct of elections in such State.

(2) A Deputy Supervisor of Elections of a State shall,
subject to the general direction and control of the Supervisor
of Elections, have all the pdwers and perform all the duties
of the Supervisor of Electidns in the State for which he is
appointed.

(3) An assistant returning officer shall, subject to the
general direction and control\of the returning officer whom
he is appointed to assist, have all the powers and may per-
form all the duties of such returning officer; and any
reference to a returning officer in this Ordinance or any
regulation made thereunder shall unless the context other-
wise requires be deemed to include a reference to an assistant
returning officer.

(4) (a) If any returning officer is by sickness or other
cause prevented or disabled from performing any of his
duties under this Ordinance and there is not time for any
other person to be appointed by the Election Commission
the returning officer may appoint\a deputy to act for him.

(b) Every appointment under paragraph (a) of this sub-
section shall as soon as possible be reported to the Election
Commission and may be revoked by the Commission but
without prejudice to the validity of anything already done
by such deputy.

(a) exercise general conitrol and supervision over the

(b) have power to issue to election officers such

(c) have power to administer any oath required to be

(d) execute and perform all other powers and duties
which are conferred or imposed upon it by this

(2) The Election Commission| may delegate, subject to
such conditions and restrictions as the Commission may

Provided that—

(a) nothing in this sub-section shall apply to any power
to make regulations under this Ordinance; and

(5) no such delegation shall affect the exercise of such
powers or the performance of such duties by the
Commission.

ParT III
REGISTRATION OF ELECTORS

8. (1) The Election Commission may, subject to the pro-
visions of Clause (1) of| Article 115 of the Constitution,
appoint a Chief Registering Officer for the Federation, a
Deputy Chief Registering Officer for each State, and a
registering officer and revising officer for each constituency.

(2) The Chief Registering Officer shall, subject to the
direction and control of the Election Commission, exercise
general direction and supervsion over all matters relating
to the registration of electors.

(3) A Deputy Chief Registering Officer shall, subject to
the general direction and supervision of the Chief Register-
ing Officer have and exercise all the powers of the Chief
Registering Officer in the State for which he is appointed.

9. (1) Each registering officer shall prepare, publish and
revise in the prescribed manner an electoral roll for the
constituency for which he is appointed.

(2) The electoral rolls for Parliamentary electors and
State electors shall, unless the Election Commission shall
otherwise direct, be combined|in a single register.

10. No person shall be entitled to be entered on the electoral
roll as an elector in more than one constituency for the
purposes of the elections for Which such constituency has
been delimited.

11. For the purposes of Article 119 of the Constitution
the qualifying date, that is to say, the date by reference to
which the electoral rolls are prepared or revised, shall be
the date immediately preceding |the commencement of the
period, determined in accordance with regulations made
under this Ordinance, during which application may be
made for registration on the electoral roll as a Parliamentary
or State elector, or such other date as the Election Commis-
sion may by notification in the Gazette appoint.

ParT IV
CONDUCT OF ELECTIONS

12. (1) For the purposes of every \general election and of
any bye-election, the Election Commission shall issue writs
addressed to the returning officer of each constituency for
which a member is to be elected.

(2) Every writ issued under sub-se¢tion (1) shall be in the
prescribed form.                 |

(3) A writ for a bye-electidn shall be issued not later than
twenty days after the occurrence of the vacancy which is to
be filled at such bye-electiop.

(4) Upon receipt of a writ issued under sub-section (1),
the returning officer shall proceed to hold an election in the
prescribed manner.

13. (1) Subject to the provisions of the Election Offences
Ordinance, 1954, the candidate for a constituency who polls
the greatest number of valid votes cast by the electors of
such constituency shall be deemed to be the elected member
for such constituency :

(a) whenever only one candidate stands nominated in
any constituency such nominated candidate shall
be deemed to be the elected member for such
